questions.q: What does GROUP BY ROLLUP (Color, Size) add on top of a plain GROUP BY Color, Size?
options: A subtotal row per Color, plus one grand total row
A subtotal row per Size, plus one grand total row
No extra rows — it just reorders the existing groups
A separate result set for each column
questions.explain: ROLLUP peels columns off right to left — it adds a subtotal per Color (Size shown as NULL), then one grand total row (both NULL).

questions.q: In GROUP BY ROLLUP (Color, Size), which column determines the broader subtotal level?
options: Color — because it was listed first, and ROLLUP rolls up right to left
Size — because it was listed second
Whichever column has fewer distinct values
SQL Server decides automatically based on a real hierarchy in the data
questions.explain: ROLLUP has no knowledge of your data's real structure — it strictly follows the order you list the columns in, rolling up right to left.

questions.q: Why can't you just check 'IS NULL' on the Color column to find ROLLUP's subtotal rows?
options: Because some products genuinely have a NULL Color in the real data, so a NULL could mean either thing
Because ROLLUP never produces NULL values
Because IS NULL doesn't work in GROUP BY queries
Because Color is never NULL in AdventureWorks2012
questions.explain: Production.Product has real NULL Color values, so a NULL alone can't distinguish a genuine missing value from a ROLLUP-generated subtotal.

questions.q: What does GROUPING(Color) return for a ROLLUP subtotal row where Color shows NULL because of the rollup, not the data?
questions.explain: GROUPING() returns 1 specifically when that column's NULL was generated by ROLLUP/CUBE, and 0 for any ordinary group value, including a real NULL from the data.

questions.q: In a result row with GROUPING(Color) = 0 and GROUPING(Size) = 1 from GROUP BY ROLLUP (Color, Size), what kind of row is it?
options: A Color subtotal — every size, for one specific color
A plain detail row for one exact Color/Size combination
An error — this combination can't occur
questions.explain: GROUPING(Color)=0 means Color is a real group value; GROUPING(Size)=1 means Size was rolled up — exactly the Color-subtotal level ROLLUP produces.
